sources.note: Silent on stress: 'Kuvi language has 27 segmental phonemes (5 vowels and 22 consonants) and 2 supra-segmental phonemes.. Two suprasegmental features, namely, length and nasalisation are found to occur in this [language]'. Data from Laxmipur (northern/Rayagada dialect).

sources.citation: Behera, Laxmidhar & Jagannath Dash. 2026. 'Kui' and 'Kuvi' Kondhs of Odisha: a comparative study of their language and culture. IOSR Journal of Humanities and Social Science 31(5) ser. 4: 13-22. doi:10.9790/0837-3105041322
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: 'Stress in Kuvi is generally non-phonemic, and intonation patterns are used primarily for pragmatic and discourse-level functions.' Anthropological overview without data or page-cited sources; bibliography contains a fabricated reference (Anderson & Harrison 2008 'South Munda Languages: Kui and Kuvi'), so not usable as a description of record. No placement statement anyway.

sources.note: Fullest modern grammar of Kuvi; Google Books snippets prove it speaks of 'a stressed syllable' and 'syllables carrying phonetic stress', so it almost certainly states where (phonetic, non-phonemic) stress falls. HathiTrust has it digitized search-only (Record 000122266, uva.x002705745); Harvard Widener PL4706.I87x 1979 eligible for a library scan.

sources.note: Snippet: 'KUI [dialects.. Kui, Konda-Kui, Manda-Kui, Kui-Kuvi]. Madhya Pradesh (India). • Primary stress falls on the initial syllable.' This is the KUI entry (kuii1252), which merely lists 'Kui-Kuvi' among alternate/dialect names; there is no separate Kuvi entry. StressTyp2 SQL dump held by the project has only an ISO row for kxv, no Kuvi record; WALS (held by the project) has no stress features coded for Kuvi.
